title: Splitting finite etale covers of universal residual henselian root algebras
statement:
Let $S$ be a nonempty connected affine scheme and let $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point. Let $S_\infty=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be the inverse limit of a small cofinal system of all pointed connected finite etale Galois covers of $(S,s)$ with pointed transition maps [lem-sfb-pointed-finite-etale-limit-cover]. Let $H$ be a commutative ring, $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in H$ with $r\geq0$, and $J=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. Assume that $(H,J)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and fix an isomorphism $H/J\cong R$. For any integer $n\geq1$ put
$$H_n=H[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n-t_i)_i,\qquad C_n=H_n/JH_n\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(x_i^n)_i,\qquad K_n=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\subset C_n.$$
Then every finite etale scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, including finite etale schemes not initially specified as pullbacks of covers of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. The algebra $H_n$ is finite free over $H$ with basis $\{\prod_i x_i^{a_i}:0\leq a_i<n\}$. The pairs $(H_n,JH_n)$ and $(C_n,K_n)$ are henselian, $C_n/K_n\cong R$, and $K_n^{r(n-1)+1}=0$. Every finite etale $E\to\operatorname{Spec}H_n$ admits an isomorphism
$$E\cong\coprod_{a\in A}\operatorname{Spec}H_n$$
for a finite set $A$. More precisely, every isomorphism $E\times_{H_n}R\cong\coprod_A\operatorname{Spec}R$ lifts uniquely first over $C_n$ and then over $H_n$, including the inverse map. No Noetherian or local hypothesis on $H$, $R$ or $H_n$ is imposed, and $r=0$ and $A=\varnothing$ are allowed.

proof.text: Pointed morphisms between connected Galois covers are unique because evaluation at the marked fibre point is injective. Thus the existing small category indexing the universal cover is thin. Its thin skeleton is an equivalent preorder; its order dual is directed by cofilteredness. Whisker the existing limit cone along this equivalence. The stages and transitions are affine, and the stages are qcqs. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-data-descent] to any finite etale E over the limit, obtaining an etale finitely presented stage model. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite] to its structure morphism: after refinement the model is also finite. Pullback composition gives a cartesian square identifying E with its base change. No descent from S is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, lemma-limit, proof: Limits Tags 01ZM, 01ZO and 07RP; directed cofinal pointed indexing as in the stated limit

proof.text: Compose the finite etale stage model with its finite etale map to S, using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Each geometric fibre point of E induces a point of this composite. The existing universal cover map to that composite has this prescribed marked value. Marked uniqueness, applied to the indexing stage, makes it compatible with the limit projection. The cartesian square therefore yields a section of E taking the marked point to the chosen fibre point. Form the coproduct of these sections. On geometric fibres it is bijective: a map from the one-point spectrum of the algebraically closed field into a coproduct factors through a summand, whose structure map forces its map to the base to be the marked point; the section label is recovered by evaluation. The geometric fibre functor of finite etale covers over the connected limit is conservative, so this coproduct map is an isomorphism. Reindex its finite label set by a lifted Fin m. This includes the empty fibre.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, lemma-limit, followed by the pointed splitting; Morphisms Tags 01WK, 02GN; agent graph-and-clopen argument

proof.text: For each parameter use the monic polynomial X^n-t_i and its AdjoinRoot power basis [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free]. Construct mutually inverse algebra maps between the finite tensor product of these algebras and the actual simultaneous multivariable quotient, sending coefficients and roots to the corresponding coefficients and roots. Transport the tensor product of the power bases; its pure tensor formula is precisely the required monomial formula. Construct the residual isomorphism and the quotient-by-roots isomorphism by explicit coefficient and root maps, prove their inverses by quotient and polynomial extensionality, and verify the coefficient and root equations. The residual roots have nth power zero. The binomial formula gives (I sup J)^(a+b+1) <= I^(a+1) sup J^(b+1); finite induction on the root generators proves K_n^(r(n-1)+1)=0. Empty tensor products and the zero ideal handle r=0.

source.place: Monic division, as in Tag 04GG, lemma-characterize-henselian, proof (10) implies (1); agent iteration and monomial count

proof.text: The finite free algebra $H_n$ is a finite $H$-module, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] makes $H\to H_n$ integral. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-over-henselian-pair] to the given henselian pair $(H,J)$. It follows that $(H_n,JH_n)$ is henselian. Both statements allow arbitrary commutative rings, so this step uses neither locality nor a Noetherian assumption.

A nilpotent ideal I makes the ring I-adically separated and complete: if I^N=0, the separation condition already holds at N, and an I-adic Cauchy sequence is constant from N onward; its Nth term is a limit at every smaller power as well. Apply this to the displayed nilpotence of K_n and use Mathlib's IsAdicComplete-to-HenselianRing instance. This gives (C_n,K_n) directly, including K_n=0.

source.place: Tags 0544, lemma-locally-nilpotent, and 00J9, lemma-lift-idempotents; More on Algebra Tag 0ALI, lemma-locally-nilpotent-henselian

proof.text: The trivial finite coproduct is finite by the library finite-coproduct instance and etale by [lem-sc-etale-coproduct-etale]. Universality of finite coproducts supplies the canonical pullback comparison with the trivial cover of the new base. A finite etale cover over R splits by step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-restriction-fully-faithful] to the identity proper morphism over (C_n,K_n), using the explicitly constructed quotient isomorphism to R. Full faithfulness, together with the fully faithful forgetful functor to the over category, yields a bijection on isomorphisms; take its inverse to lift any specified residual isomorphism uniquely. Repeat for (H_n,JH_n), where the quotient is definitionally C_n. This gives both specified successive unique lifts and, by choosing a residual splitting, the splitting over H_n. No choice of an arbitrary algebra witness is used.

All six steps check out against the full statements of the 19 cited nodes. Step 1: re-indexing by the directed system of open normal subgroups is justified by cor-galois-open-subgroups and thm-galois-fundamental. An arbitrary finite etale E over T is etale of finite presentation; clause (1) of etale-finite-data-descent gives W_i, and descend-finite (S_0=Y_i, f_0 etale so locally of finite type) gives a finite stage. This matches pione 0BTV (line 3428) and limits 01ZO (line 1772). Step 2: the composite W_j to S is finite etale, so limit-cover splits W_j x_S T.
